submission.justification: Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c across thicknesses: R3 peaks near 2.5 cm (4.61-4.72 sigma, 4.72 at 3 cm) but its documents give no lifetime protection, while R1 is the only candidate with a documented stability feature (hydrophobic treatment, relevant to porous-aerogel moisture uptake; the gas volume is dry nitrogen). R1 peaks near 3 cm at 3.84 sigma (3.64 at 2 cm, 3.55 at 4 cm, 2.62 at 6 cm). R2 is lower (max ~2.9 sigma). I chose R1 at 3 cm, which trades about 0.9 sigma of separation against R3 for the lifetime constraint. This choice rests on the hydrophobic treatment as a design feature; no aging or humidity test data were found for any candidate, so lifetime performance is not measured. R3 remains the best option if aging data show it is stable.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 gives the highest separation (4.72 sigma at 3 cm), above the chosen R1 (3.84 sigma at 3 cm). Recommending R1 is a deliberate trade-off for the lifetime constraint, so the goal is only partly met.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is a listed candidate (porous with hydrophobic treatment).

requirements.requirement: Performance maintained over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: R1 has a hydrophobic treatment, the only documented stability feature among the candidates; gas volume is dry nitrogen. No measured aging data exist, so this is inferred from design rather than verified.

requirements.requirement: Submit one recommended radiator and thickness
